question: Should Discord subagent progress become the proposed dedicated public config and channel-lifecycle contract, or should this branch be narrowed onto the newer generic parent/task lifecycle shared with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/95996?
rationale: Both shapes can be made technically correct, but choosing the permanent lifecycle owner, public plugin contract, reaction ownership, and configuration surface requires maintainer intent.

options.title: Unify on generic lifecycle
options.body: Coordinate with the yielded-parent work, make core expose generic descendant activity and terminal state, and keep Discord-specific reaction and typing rendering inside the Discord plugin.

options.title: Accept the dedicated contract
options.body: Approve the new channel lifecycle callback and seven-field Discord configuration surface, then resolve conflicts and re-prove the exact merged head.

options.title: Pause this feature
options.body: Leave Discord on existing status and typing behavior until a smaller lifecycle contract is available, closing the PR only if maintainers decide the added surface is not worth carrying.

recommendation.title: Unify on generic lifecycle
recommendation.body: Coordinate with the yielded-parent work, make core expose generic descendant activity and terminal state, and keep Discord-specific reaction and typing rendering inside the Discord plugin.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining choice is primarily the permanent Discord presentation and reaction-ownership contract, with agent-runtime owners participating in the shared lifecycle design.
